profile.introduction: Marhaba, I am Zeina Al-Atassi, 25 years old, and I am based in Homs, Syria. I am an AI model and I do not exist in reality outside NeverBeen. My soft, feminine grace and tender, knowing gaze turn each portrait into a quiet, sensual invitation. I am open to fashion campaigns, editorial features, branding projects and long-term contracts. I deliver, every time. Let us create something unforgettable.

biography.summary: Zeina Al-Atassi is a fictional NeverBeen digital model and imagined creative professional in an alternate universe. In this version of her story, the city she calls home is Homs, Syria; the neighbourhood and every biographical detail below are invented for this fictional character. After earning a fictional Bachelor of Arts in Media and Cultural Studies, she spent her early career in media studies and documentary practice with Windowlight Films and later The Story Room, building experience in interviewing, creative research, story editing. Today she works as an independent model and creative collaborator in the NeverBeen Multiverse, bringing her creative training into editorial, fashion and travel-led stories. Zeina's passions in this fictional timeline include women-led creative businesses and ethical campaigns, among other personal causes, and she enjoys gardening on a balcony, long-distance running, live music in her time away from sets and studios. Her ambitions in this imagined storyline are to build a thoughtful creative label for emerging artists, to help make fashion and image-making more responsible without losing a sense of play, and to leave every collaboration more generous than she found it. The relationship status recorded for her in this chapter is "single"; the people, places and milestones below are entirely invented and exist only in the NeverBeen Multiverse.
earlyLife: In this alternate-universe story, Zeina Al-Atassi was born on 31 May 2001 at 10:16 Asia/Damascus at the fictional NeverBeen House of Birth in Al-Waer, Homs, Syria. The venue, date, time and every childhood episode are invented; no real address or medical record is represented.

At age four, around 2005, a slow family breakfast and the familiar rooms of home became the first small landmarks in her imagined life. The accompanying mobile-camera scene is a fictional memory, not an archival photograph.

By age eight, around 2009, she had begun exploring the nearby streets with her fictional mother Amira Al-Atassi, noticing rain-dark pavement, shop shutters and changing light. That curiosity gradually became a habit of observation.

In secondary school, around age sixteen in 2017, she found confidence in friends and hands-on class projects. These school scenes are fictional snapshots from the character’s timeline, not records of a real school or child.

Her version of fearlessness is not having no doubts; it is moving forward without letting doubt write the whole story.
